==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|longitude}}, from {{der|en|la|longitūdō||length, a measured length}}, from {{m|la|longus||long}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{a|en|RP|Aus|NZ}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈlɒnd͡ʒɪtʃuːd/|a=yod-coalescence}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈlɒŋɡɪtjuːd/|a=non-<<yod-coalescence>>}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈlɒnd͡ʒɪtjuːd/|a=more traditional}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈlɑnd͡ʒəˌtud/|/ˈlɔnd͡ʒəˌtud/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-longitude.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|en-GB-longitude.ogg|a=UK}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|geography}} [[angular|Angular]] [[distance]] measured west or east of the [[prime meridian]].
#: {{cot|en|latitude}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2012-03
|author=William E. Carter; Merri Sue Carter
|title=The British Longitude Act Reconsidered
|volume=100|issue=2|page=87
|magazine=w:American Scientist
|url=http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/the-british-longitude-act-reconsidered
|passage=But was it responsible governance to pass the '''Longitude''' Act without other efforts to protect British seamen? Or might it have been subterfuge—a disingenuous attempt to shift attention away from the realities of their life at sea.}}
# {{lb|en|geography|astronomy}} Any imaginary [[line]] [[perpendicular]] to the [[equator]] and part of a [[great circle]] passing through the [[North Pole]] and [[South Pole]].
#: {{syn|en|meridian}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}} [[length|Length]].
#* {{quote-book|en|passage=His shoulders are remarkably sloping, giving an appearance of great '''longitude''' to his neck.
|pageurl=http://books.google.ca/books?id=-MdPAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA504&dq=%22great+longitude%22&lr=&as_brr=0&ei=iGOHT_DJCZTcNYDmlJQD&cd=13&redir_esc=y#v=onepage&q=%22great%20longitude%22&f=false
|page=504
|title=The American Quarterly Review
|volume=10
|year=1831
|chapter=Griffin's Remains
|author=Francis Griffin}}
